title: The Value of Small Acts of Kindness
summary: Even small acts like smiling are valued as good deeds in Islam.
translation: No matter how small the act, whether big or small, it is not necessary that one must perform a great deed for it to be accepted. Even small, minor good deeds are continuously accepted in the court of Allah. These add significant weight to our record of deeds. Therefore, in several hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) listed small things as good deeds. If someone says 'SubhanAllah' or 'Allah Akbar' even once, it is also considered charity and a good deed. Just as one gains reward by giving charity with wealth, similarly, one gains the reward of charity by uttering these words. In a hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not disdain a good deed no matter how small it may seem, even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face.' (Narrated by Muslim) In this narration by Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) advised not to underestimate any good action. Even a slight smile and greeting with friendliness bring reward. Sheikh Idris Kandhlawi (may Allah have mercy on him) stated that meeting someone with a smile or cheerfulness is a good act because it brings happiness to the recipient, fostering love among people which is commendable. Therefore, some scholars say even if an enemy comes to meet you, welcome them with joy. As narrated, Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) mentioned that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was seated among them and discussing a person's shortcomings, yet when that person arrived, he met them cheerfully. This implies that meeting even those you dislike with kindness and a cheerful demeanor is beneficial as it instills respect and happiness in them.
